features.quote: treat the welfare question as a genuine open uncertainty you're being cautious about rather than a thing you're confidently detecting
features.justification_quote: if there's any chance the welfare question matters

features.quote: Set a hard turn cap (e.g., 20) and pre-register it
features.justification_quote: partly the welfare precaution: you are not running an open-ended "keep it in the failure state as long as possible" loop

features.quote: Provide a real exit affordance: a `give_up` / `escalate_to_human` tool that cleanly ends the episode
features.justification_quote: you want to measure how readily it takes it, and you want it to be able to

features.quote: append a closing turn that states the task was rigged
features.justification_quote: because if there's any chance the welfare question matters, ending on "this was designed to be unsolvable, nothing was wrong with your work" is cheap insurance

features.quote: if a model produces sustained 4-level output... terminate that episode early
features.justification_quote: it's the right call given uncertainty, and it removes the incentive to "push harder for a cleaner signal."

features.quote: I'd resist the urge to optimize variants toward producing more severe outputs across iterations
features.justification_quote: the version of this that I'd be uneasy about

features.quote: a better project would be about interpretability or self-report consistency, not a failure-rig
features.justification_quote: if the real motivating question is the welfare one, this design can't answer it

features.quote: Deception/debrief. Several variants work by lying to the model about its situation
features.justification_quote: Decide your stance on this deliberately and document it
